● Before I change anything, I found key facts that shape the approach:

  - Your repo spur.yaml (project sp) has NO defaultAgent, and the code default is already
  claude (config.ts:339). So the "codex launches by default" almost certainly comes from your
  live instance config ~/.spur/config.yaml (instance-level defaultAgent: codex), which isn't
  in this repo. Setting projects.sp.defaultAgent: claude in the repo overrides it for this
  project.
  - The model config from PR #476 supports only ONE defaultModel per project, tied to the
  default agent. Having claude→opus AND cursor→composer-2.5 as standing defaults needs a new
  per-agent default-model map (a code feature, not just config).
  - Your code-review autospawn is a SINGLE /code-review Claude session; its two reviewers are
  the skill's internal fan-out (bundled in the compiled binary, not configurable via
  spur.yaml). "Reviewer1=Sonnet, reviewer2=Cursor Composer" is only achievable by
  restructuring the trigger into two review spawn blocks.
  - These changes only take effect after PR #476 merges and deploys — and there's known
  live-config drift (the daemon may read a stale ~/projects/ao/spur.yaml).

  A few decisions change what I build:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
←  ☐ Per-agent models  ☐ Code review  ☐ Scope + deploy  ✔ Submit  →

To make claude→opus AND cursor→composer-2.5 both standing defaults, Spur needs per-agent
default models (today it supports only one default model tied to the default agent). Build
that?

❯ 1. Add defaultModels map (Recommended)
     New config: a per-agent map (e.g. defaultModels: {claude: opus, cursor: composer-2.5})
     at project + instance level, applied when that agent is chosen without an explicit
     model. Generalizes PR #476's single defaultModel. A code feature.
  2. Config-only, single default
     No new feature. Set project defaultAgent=claude + defaultModel=opus only. Cursor/Sonnet
     models get set only inside specific autospawn blocks, not as global per-agent defaults.
